deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 62v is a printed page, numbered 12, from a Berlin University lecture catalogue ('Verzeichniss der Vorlesungen'). It continues the section on public academic institutions from the previous page (p. 11). It contains no handwriting by Riemann: no formulas, no marginalia, no calculations. The faint marks in the lower half are bleed-through or paper flaws.

Content of the page:
(a) The scientific collections are used in lectures and may be visited by students who register at the proper office.
(b) Exegetical exercises of the theological seminar: New Testament under Twesten, Old Testament under Hengstenberg; church and dogma history under Neander.
(c) Medical teaching facilities: two medical-surgical polyclinics, one in the university building and one in the University Clinic at Ziegelstraße 6; the clinic for surgery and ophthalmology, also at Ziegelstraße; the obstetric clinic at Dorotheenstraße 1-2 with its polyclinic; and the Charité clinics (medical, surgical, ophthalmological, syphilitic, obstetric and paediatric), plus the institute for forensic medicine.
(d) Philological seminar: Böckh has Sophocles read on Wednesdays and Saturdays 10-11; Lachmann has the Odes of Horace read on Wednesdays and Fridays 9-10.

Dating, my inference: Neander died in July 1850 and Lachmann in March 1851, so the catalogue predates 1850/51. Schott's Finnish/Kalevala lectures and the docents Dieterici and Wetzstein on the previous page also point to the late 1840s. This fits Riemann's student years in Berlin (1847-1849). The sheet was evidently kept by Riemann and later reused. The next folio carries his handwritten Göttingen notice of 26 April 1862 announcing lectures on partial differential equations. This suggests the catalogue sheet served as scrap or wrapper paper.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed university lecture catalogue with no mathematical content and no annotation by Riemann. Its only interest is biographical: it is probably a souvenir of his Berlin student period, c. 1847-49.
transcription_corrections: 'Ziegelstrafse' should read 'Ziegelstraße'; the print uses long-s plus s, which the machine transcription rendered as 'fs'.
'Dorotheenstrafse' should read 'Dorotheenstraße' for the same reason.
Otherwise the transcription matches the printed text. Note that the page contains no handwritten material.
